summary: Etsy's wrongful photo-copy flags are a real pain, but nothing shows a third-party timestamp changes Etsy's decision or that sellers would pay for one. Sellers also only feel the pain after a flag, when it's too late to have timestamped anything.

demand.evidence: One trade article plus forum thread titles. No evidence anyone pays for or asks for dated proof; RESEARCH admits no source shows sellers paying for appeal help.

statusQuo.evidence: Support emails, forum advocates, or relisting and losing reviews. Real cost, but the decision sits inside Etsy's automated process.

specificity.evidence: Buyer is a clear solo handmade shop with a Star Seller badge, but nobody has been spoken to and value and pain arrive at different moments.

wedge.evidence: The $9 post-flag packet is cheap to build but useless to a seller with no earlier dated originals; the prevention subscription is hard to sell.

futureFit.evidence: Etsy may add its own appeal route or attestation; a third-party vault depends on Etsy and the copy sweep costs more than the price.

premises: Wrongly flagged handmade sellers exist in volume (one article)
They would pay $9 once or $12 a month (unsupported)
Independent RFC 3161 timestamps influence Etsy's review (unsupported, central)
Sellers will upload before being flagged (weak)
A timestamp proves existence, not authorship (true, limits value)
alternatives: Minimal: free guide and checklist on timestamping photos with FreeTSA plus appeal tips
Ideal: vault plus Etsy API plus weekly copy sweep (L effort, sweep exceeds zero cost)
Lateral: interview 5 flagged sellers and the VAR-named advocate before building anything
No existing repo of David's to extend; proofpack is the closest and was passed
wedge: A $9 one-off packet for a seller who was just flagged and already has dated originals, which is rarely the case.

feasibility.notes: Next.js, Supabase free, FreeTSA, pdf-lib, exifr. Proving test: upload a JPEG and openssl ts -verify on the stored .tsr exits 0, with a one-byte change reporting MISMATCH. The M3 copy sweep is not zero-cost.

risks: Etsy may give timestamps no weight
Pain arrives after the moment the product must be used
Etsy may fix the bot or add an appeal route
Reverse-image sweep costs more than the plan price
killCriteria: Drop it if no seller or advocate says an independent timestamp would be attached or considered, or fewer than 5 of 30 sellers say they would pay $9 in a two-week test.
